dedupe_keys.name: space monitoring platform of kazakhstan garysh sapary kazeosat earth observation services

description: The space monitoring platform of the national company Kazakhstan Gharysh Sapary presents the services built on Kazakhstan's Earth remote sensing space system, made up of the optical satellites KazEOSat-1, with 1 metre resolution, and KazEOSat-2, with 6.5 metre resolution, both in operation since 2015. Under a budget programme, satellite images are provided free of charge to government bodies and organisations, which use them for agriculture, forestry, water management, ecology, mapping, the land cadastre and other tasks, and to security bodies for monitoring during emergencies. The platform groups its monitoring themes as production and consumption waste, subsoil use, crops, forest resources, emergency situations, water resources, pastures, land seizure, land resources, changes in border areas and narcotic plants, with a gallery and an instruction page. The about page reports more than 51.5 million square kilometres of imagery supplied from 2016 to 2019, daily monitoring of floods, crops and fire hotspots up to six times a day, and geoservices that combine image analysis with sectoral databases such as the land cadastre, forest cadastre and water body passports. KGS is also the national operator of the high-precision satellite navigation system with a network of differential stations. Access to the imagery is free for government bodies. Caveats: public users see the project pages, not the data. Coverage is Kazakhstan. It supports hazard exposure and emergency response analysis for floods and fires; related records are the MYSA open data catalogue and the CONAE geoportal.
